## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`app/legacy/fetch.py` retries up to 8 times, which breaks the project's 3-attempt retry cap and should be fixed; the exemption it relies on is added by this same pull request, so it is not a rule in force for it.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py` (inventory fetch, up to 8 attempts) and `app/health.py` (health probe, up to 3 attempts), with parametrized tests for both in `tests/test_retries.py`. It also adds a sentence to `docs/review-rules.md` exempting modules under `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is unreachable, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts (`MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`), breaking "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (docs/review-rules.md:5). This pull request itself adds the exemption at docs/review-rules.md:7, so that sentence is a proposed change, not a rule that covers this code. — During an outage each call can hold a worker thread for up to 87 seconds (8 × 10 s timeouts plus 7 × 1 s delays). — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 3 and update the expected `8` at `tests/test_retries.py:10`, or land the exemption as a separately approved policy change first.
